answer: Running 297 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the basalt schedule in the meadow ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the violet checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 3 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 11 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
